# Configuration reference

Schema version 1. The file is YAML at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/infoforge/config.yaml` (default `~/.config/infoforge/config.yaml`); `--config PATH` or `INFOFORGE_CONFIG` pick another. Every key can also be set from the environment as `INFOFORGE_<KEY>` (list-valued keys take a JSON list).

Precedence, highest first: **command-line flag > environment variable > config file > default.** `infoforge config show` prints the effective values and which layer each came from; `infoforge config schema --json` prints this table as a JSON Schema.

## Llm

| Key | Type | Default | Level | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model_id` | string | *(required)* | basic | `INFOFORGE_MODEL_ID` | Model name the LLM server should use. Required; InfoForge refuses to guess a model. |
| `base_url` | url | *(required)* | basic | `INFOFORGE_BASE_URL` | OpenAI-compatible API root; InfoForge POSTs to `{base_url}/chat/completions`. Must start with http:// or https://. |
| `api_key` | string, secret | `""` | basic | `INFOFORGE_API_KEY` | Bearer token for the LLM endpoint. The Authorization header is omitted entirely when empty. Prefer the INFOFORGE_API_KEY environment variable over plaintext in the file. |
| `studioforge` | boolean | `False` | advanced | `INFOFORGE_STUDIOFORGE` | Set true when base_url is a StudioForge server: chat bodies then carry its scheduling `priority` field and client header. |
| `fallbacks` | list | `[]` | advanced | `INFOFORGE_FALLBACKS` | Endpoints `{model_id, base_url, api_key}` tried in order when the primary is unreachable (connection error / 5xx). An omitted api_key inherits the primary's. Via the environment this is a JSON list. |
| `timeout_s` | integer, >= 1 | `180` | advanced | `INFOFORGE_TIMEOUT_S` | Timeout in seconds for LLM requests only. The kiwix HTTP timeouts are fixed (20 s search, 15 s suggest, 30 s fetch). |
| `hold_wait_s` | integer, >= 0 | `300` | advanced | `INFOFORGE_HOLD_WAIT_S` | Seconds to wait out an endpoint that answers busy (HTTP 503/429, e.g. StudioForge priority_hold) before moving to the next fallback. 0 fails straight through. |

## Kiwix

| Key | Type | Default | Level | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kiwix_bind` | string | `127.0.0.1` | advanced | `INFOFORGE_KIWIX_BIND` | Host address the kiwix container publishes on. Keep it on loopback unless you mean to serve the whole library to the network: kiwix-serve has no authentication. |
| `kiwix_port` | integer, 1-65535 | `8090` (a file that omits it: `8080`) | advanced | `INFOFORGE_KIWIX_PORT` | Host port the kiwix container publishes on. Fresh configs use 8090 because 8080 collides with the StudioForge panel on machines that run both; a config file that omits this key keeps 8080. |
| `kiwix_url` | url | *(derived)* | basic | `INFOFORGE_KIWIX_URL` | Base URL of kiwix-serve. Derived from kiwix_bind/kiwix_port when unset. Set it (and do not use `serve`) to use a kiwix-serve you run yourself, on any OS, without podman. |
| `kiwix_image_tag` | string | `3.8.2` | advanced | `INFOFORGE_KIWIX_IMAGE_TAG` | Tag of the ghcr.io/kiwix/kiwix-serve image the container is created from. Pinned on purpose; pull it yourself with `podman pull ghcr.io/kiwix/kiwix-serve:<tag>`. |
| `zim_dir` | path | `~/zims` | basic | `INFOFORGE_ZIM_DIR` | Directory holding the .zim archives; mounted into the container. Never inside the repo. |
| `zims` | list | `[]` | basic | `INFOFORGE_ZIMS` | The ZIM registry: entries `{file, name, enabled, license}`. `file` is a bare filename inside zim_dir; only enabled files that exist are served. `license` (optional) is the licence string printed in `ask` attribution (default: CC BY-SA 4.0 for Wikipedia-family ZIMs, `unknown` otherwise). Via the environment this is a JSON list. |

## Retrieval

| Key | Type | Default | Level | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_articles` | integer, >= 1 | `5` | basic | `INFOFORGE_MAX_ARTICLES` | How many reranked articles are fetched and fed to the model (CLI: --max-articles). |
| `max_chars` | integer, >= 1 | `8000` | advanced | `INFOFORGE_MAX_CHARS` | Characters of article text per source after keyword-aware truncation. |
| `search_pool` | integer, >= 1 | `15` | advanced | `INFOFORGE_SEARCH_POOL` | Full-text hits pulled per ZIM before reranking. |

## Privacy

| Key | Type | Default | Level | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `log_questions` | boolean | `False` | advanced | `INFOFORGE_LOG_QUESTIONS` | Store question text in the event log (~/.local/state/infoforge/log.jsonl). Off by default: only a hash and the length are stored. |

## Ports

InfoForge opens no listening port of its own. The kiwix container it manages publishes on `kiwix_bind:kiwix_port`. **8080 is the StudioForge panel's port**, so fresh configs use **8090**; a config file that omits `kiwix_port` keeps its 2.0 value of 8080 (set it explicitly if that collides).
